text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- More than 192,000 people were unemployed in Switzerland at the end of December, a new record high, and the rise is expected to continue.

- Abraham Burg, president of the Jewish Agency, refuses to meet with Thomas Borer, Swiss diplomat and head of the "Task Force for Funds of Nazi Victims" because of a recent remark made by former Swiss President Delamuraz calling Jewish demands
- Vorarlberger Volksbank of Austria became the first foreign bank to open a branch in the canton of St. Gallen.
- Swiss Metal Group suffered a 12 percent sales decline to 315 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- Helsana Insurance AG took over insurance firm Patria Allgemeine on January 1 and named the new company Helsana Unfall (Accident).
- Walter Hefti replaces resigning Robert Haab as Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann president.
- A Swiss man received a life sentence on the Maledives shortly after his arrival there when customs officials found three hemp seeds in his suitcase.
